questionText: Which of the following best describes the first step in the six-step approach to building a sustainable supply chain?
options: Identifying external trends and future developments
Stocktaking the current state of company and supply chain strategies, practices, resources, and capabilities
Evaluating risks and opportunities from internal and external factors
Implementing a Sustainable Supply Chain Scorecard

questionText: A procurement manager personally believes that sustainability is essential for the future of the planet and consistently chooses suppliers based on their environmental and social records, even when it requires extra effort. This behavior best represents which level of the affective domain?

A supply chain strategist is designing a completely new closed-loop system that not only reduces waste but also generates revenue from recycled materials, while redefining industry standards for sustainable production. This innovative design process is at which cognitive level?

A logistics manager feels personally committed to reducing carbon emissions and voluntarily initiates a program to switch to electric delivery vehicles, even though it is not required by law or company policy. This attitude reflects which level of the affective domain?
What is the primary focus of sustainable procurement according to the text?
options: Only reducing costs in the supply chain
Inclusion of sustainability issues in procurement strategy and decisions, covering the triple bottom line
Limiting procurement to local suppliers only

questionText: In the six-step approach, what is the main purpose of Step 2 (Your Environment: Current, Potential, and Future Impact Factors)?
options: To evaluate internal resources and capabilities
To identify potential risks and opportunities from external factors such as stakeholders and input resources
To implement a new supply chain strategy

questionText: Which of the following is an example of a strategic SSC program focused on differentiation, first mover advantage, and establishing market entry barriers?
According to the text, what is the definition of cleaner production as provided by UNEP?
options: The use of end-of-pipe technology to treat pollution after it is created
The continuous application of an integrated preventive environmental strategy to processes, products, and services to increase eco-efficiency and reduce risks
The elimination of all waste through incineration
The exclusive use of renewable energy in manufacturing

questionText: What does the term "industrial symbiosis" refer to in the context of cleaner production?
options: The collaboration between competing firms to fix prices
The exchange of by-products, energy, and materials among industries to add value and reduce waste
The merger of two manufacturing companies
The use of industrial robots in production

questionText: Which of the following is a key difference between ISO 14001:2004 and EMAS?
options: EMAS does not require public reporting, while ISO 14001 does
EMAS requires compliance with environmental regulations and public reporting every three years, while ISO 14001 emphasizes commitment to compliance without mandatory public reporting
ISO 14001 is only for European companies

questionText: In the context of reverse logistics, which of the following is a key difference between new product and reverse logistics supply chains?
options: Reverse logistics has no uncertainty in product quality
Reverse logistics involves uncertain quality, quantity, and timing of returned products
New product logistics requires more inspection and separation
Reverse logistics has fewer collection points

questionText: What percentage of global carbon dioxide emissions is estimated to come from logistics activity according to the World Economic Forum?
Which of the following is a principle of environmentally friendlier packaging according to the EU directive?
options: Use maximum packaging volume to ensure safety
Design packaging for reuse, recovery, or recycling, and minimize hazardous substances
Avoid biodegradable materials at all costs
Use only virgin materials for packaging

questionText: What is the main argument made by PlasticEurope regarding the use of plastic in packaging?
options: Plastic packaging should be completely banned
Without plastic packaging, alternative materials would increase weight, GHG emissions, costs, energy use, and waste significantly
Plastic packaging has no environmental impact

questionText: In the six-step approach, what does the Threat-Opportunity Profile help supply chain managers to determine?
options: The exact cost of implementing sustainability
Strategic gaps between current strategy and the changing business environment
The number of suppliers to eliminate

questionText: Which strategic SSC program is mainly driven by additional supply chain costs due to increasing resource prices and aims for long-term improvement of effectiveness?
What is the definition of "zero waste" as described in the cleaner production section?
options: Producing no waste at all by redesigning product lifecycles or transforming waste into useful materials or energy

questionText: According to the text, which of the following is an internal driver for sustainable procurement?
options: The wish to reduce costs through reduction of waste, pollution, or litigation costs

questionText: What does the "constructive adaptation" level of internal adaptation of sustainable practices involve?
options: Embracing the integration of product and process design into sustainability planning and maximizing benefits

questionText: Which of the following is an example of an innovation solution for cleaner production in textile dyeing mentioned in the text?
options: Using more water in the dyeing process
The DyeCoo machine that uses carbon dioxide instead of water to dye polyester
Extending dyeing time to eight hours

questionText: In the context of sustainable logistics, what does the "greening" of logistical activities primarily focus on?
options: Ensuring activities are environmentally friendly, reducing carbon emissions across the supply chain
Using only one mode of transportation

questionText: Which of the following is a recommendation for shippers and buyers to green the supply chain?
options: Build environmental performance indicators into contracting with logistics service providers

questionText: What is the main purpose of the Balanced Scorecard in the context of sustainable supply chain strategy implementation?
options: To translate strategic goals into operational terms and communicate strategy across the organization
To replace the need for financial reporting

questionText: Which of the following is an external barrier to sustainable procurement?
options: Suppliers not willing to share information, preventing integration

questionText: What is the estimated annual global production of plastic according to PlasticEurope?
In the six-step approach, what is the role of scenario planning in Step 2?
options: To determine the company's current inventory levels
To explore drivers that shape the future of the supply chain and forecast probable future developments

questionText: Which strategic SSC program is driven by compliance requirements of stakeholders such as governments and special interest groups?
What is the definition of "eco-efficiency" according to the World Business Council for Sustainable Development?
options: Producing goods at the lowest possible cost regardless of environmental impact
Delivering competitively priced goods and services while progressively reducing ecological impacts and resource intensity throughout the lifecycle
Maximizing the use of non-renewable resources
Ignoring the carrying capacity of the earth

questionText: Which of the following is a characteristic of the "reactive adaptation" to sustainable practices?
options: Embracing sustainability as a competitive advantage
Complying with environmental and social responsibility law to avoid penalties, with end-of-pipe solutions

questionText: What is the main advantage of using plastic film to extend the shelf life of vegetables?
options: It reduces CO2 emissions because the environmental impact of food waste is much higher than the packaging
It requires more energy to produce than the food saves

questionText: In reverse logistics, what is one of the primary questions from a strategic perspective?
options: How to increase forward logistics speed?
What types of materials may be returned, recovered, or recycled?

questionText: Which of the following is a principle of cleaner production applied to the entire production cycle?
options: Increase the consumption of raw materials
Reduce at source the quantity and toxicity of emissions and wastes

questionText: What is the main difference between ISO 14001:2015 and the earlier version regarding environmental management?
options: The 2015 version eliminates the need for compliance
The 2015 version increases the onus on strategic planning and proactive initiatives to protect the environment, addressing the full lifecycle
The 2015 version is only for large companies

questionText: According to the text, which of the following is a driver for sustainable supply chain practices from customers?
options: Customers always prefer the lowest price regardless of sustainability
Consumer-facing companies face pressure from pressure groups and environmental campaigners, which drives sustainability improvements
Customers only buy from companies that have no environmental policies

questionText: What is the purpose of the Sustainable Supply Chain (SSC) Scorecard in Step 5?
options: To aid in the implementation of a sustainability strategy by balancing economic, environmental, and social objectives and translating strategy into KPIs

questionText: Which of the following is an example of a "Progression" strategic program action?
options: Certification of adherence to mandatory standards
Funding research institutions and establishing new standards, e.g., CO2 measurement standard
Price differentiation for premium sustainable products

questionText: What is the estimated percentage of plastic produced globally that is used for packaging?
In the context of packaging, what does MAP stand for?
Which of the following is a principle of cleaner agricultural production mentioned in the text?
options: Maximize harmful impact of crop protection practices
Promote decent work and fair labor practices

questionText: What is the main finding of the comparison between paper and plastic bags according to Science World?
options: Paper bags are always better for the environment
Production of paper bags consumes more energy and creates more pollution than plastic bags, but recycling paper consumes more energy than recycling plastic

questionText: Which of the following is a key success factor for the "Innovation" strategic program?
options: Top management commitment throughout key supply chain players and communication
Focusing only on internal cost reduction

questionText: What is the definition of "pollution prevention" according to the US EPA?
options: Treating pollution after it is created
Source reduction, preventing or reducing waste where it originates, including conservation of natural resources

questionText: In the context of reverse logistics, what is one of the uncertainties in the recovery process?
options: Uncertainty in consumer behavior and return initiation

questionText: What is the main recommendation for policy makers to green transportation infrastructure?
options: Promote expansion of integrated flow management schemes and invest in congested nodes and mode switches
Increase dependence on road transport only

questionText: Which of the following is an example of a "Re-design" strategic program action?
options: Regionalization of procurement and production structures

questionText: What is the main purpose of the EU directive for packaging and packaging waste (94/62/EC)?
options: To set principles for environmentally friendlier packaging design, production, and commercialization, including minimum volume, reuse, recovery, and minimization of hazardous substances
To require all packaging to be made of glass

questionText: According to the text, which of the following is a driver for sustainable supply chain practices from competitors?
options: Competitors may become technology leaders and set industry standards, forcing other companies to respond
Competitors always lower prices regardless of sustainability

questionText: What is the definition of "green productivity" as used by the Asian Productivity Organization?
options: A strategy for enhancing productivity and environmental performance to improve socioeconomic development, similar to cleaner production
A way to reduce product quality

questionText: Which of the following is a recommendation for logistics service providers to green buildings?
options: Encourage wider industry commitment to improve existing facilities with green technologies and develop recycling offerings
Only build new facilities in rural areas

questionText: What is the estimated turnover of the global packaging industry?

options: To understand levers and their potential impact to precisely define risks and opportunities

questionText: Which of the following is an example of a "Process Optimizations" strategic program benefit?
options: Improving productivity and efficiency, reducing supply chain costs and environmental impacts

questionText: What is the main challenge of implementing cleaner production according to the text?
options: It is always more expensive than traditional methods
It requires a shift in mindsets away from end-of-pipe solutions and command-and-control methods

questionText: Which of the following is a property of biodegradable packaging according to the EU directive?
options: It must be capable of decomposition into carbon dioxide, biomass, and water

questionText: What is the main role of public procurement in sustainable procurement according to the text?
options: To provide base demand to enable development of more sustainable products and services, especially in construction and infrastructure
To always choose the lowest bidder

questionText: In the context of sustainable logistics, what is the second question posed by Abukhader and Jonson (2004)?
options: What is the impact of logistics on the environment?
What is the impact of the environment on logistics?

questionText: Which of the following is a characteristic of the "resistant adaptation" to sustainable practices?
options: Believing sustainability is per se anti-business and only complying if there is no way around it

questionText: What is the main advantage of using lightweight plastic packaging in terms of CO2 emissions?
options: It reduces both the weight of transported goods and the amount of packaged goods that go to waste, thus reducing CO2 emissions

questionText: Which of the following is an external driver for sustainable procurement?
options: Pressure from customers and the general public

questionText: What is the definition of "reverse logistics" according to Rogers and Tibben-Lembke?
options: The forward movement of goods from origin to consumer
The process of planning, implementing, and controlling the efficient flow of materials from point of consumption to point of origin for value recovery or proper disposal
The disposal of goods in landfills
The manufacturing of new products from raw materials

questionText: Which of the following is a key success factor for the "Progression" strategic program?
options: A focused approach with concrete milestones and top-management commitment

questionText: What is the estimated percentage of plastic waste being landfilled globally?
options: Millions of tonnes, due to lack of efficient recycling systems

questionText: Which of the following is a principle of cleaner production regarding toxic materials?
options: Use as many toxic materials as possible
Eliminate as far as possible the use of toxic and dangerous materials
Increase the quantity of toxic emissions

questionText: What is the main purpose of the "Balanced Scorecard" as described by Kaplan and Norton?
options: To focus only on financial measures
To expand the set of business unit objectives beyond summary financial measures, including customer, internal processes, and learning and growth

questionText: In the context of sustainable procurement, what is a common misperception mentioned in the text?
options: The buyer is always in a stronger power position in the supply chain relationship
Sustainability has no impact on procurement

questionText: Which of the following is an example of a technology innovation for cleaner production in cotton dyeing?
options: ColorZen treatment that changes cotton's molecular composition to reduce chemicals, water, and energy

questionText: What is the main recommendation for shippers and buyers regarding packaging?
options: Agree on standards for packaging light weighting and elimination, and seek cross-industry agreements on modularization

questionText: Which of the following is a characteristic of the "receptive adaptation" to sustainable practices?
options: Starting to consider possible competitive advantages from sustainability but minimal translation into operational processes

questionText: What is the estimated amount of oil used to make 100 billion plastic bags in the US annually?
In the six-step approach, what is the main focus of Step 1 (Stocktaking)?
options: Internal factors, strategies, resources, and planned practices of the company and supply chain

questionText: Which of the following is an example of a "Compliance" strategic program action?
options: Certification of adherence to mandatory or customer-specific standards

questionText: What is the main benefit of using industrial symbiosis in Kalundborg, Denmark?
options: Saving millions of cubic meters of water through recycling and reuse in a closed cycle

questionText: Which of the following is a key component of the sustainable supply chain strategy integration process?
options: Balancing economic, environmental, and social objectives

questionText: What is the estimated number of trees cut down annually to produce 10 billion paper bags in the US?
Which of the following is a principle of cleaner production regarding energy and water?
options: Reduce the consumption of raw materials and energy used in producing one unit of product

questionText: In the context of reverse logistics, what is one of the uncertainties related to consumer behavior?
options: Consumers always return products on time
The consumer has to initiate the return and accept recovered products, which is uncertain

questionText: Which of the following is a recommendation for policy makers to promote mode switches?
options: Promote mode switches to rail, short sea, and inland waterways, and consider reopening idle rail lines

questionText: What is the main purpose of the "Innovation" strategic program?
options: To achieve differentiation by changing existing business models and creating a sustainable image

questionText: Which of the following is a key difference between forward and reverse logistics?
options: Reverse logistics involves inspection and separation that are labor-intensive and costly

questionText: What is the main advantage of using multi-layer films in MAP for meat packaging?
options: It extends shelf life from a few days to over a week, reducing food waste
It uses more energy than it saves

questionText: In the six-step approach, what is the purpose of analyzing goal conflicts in Step 1?
options: To discover whether there is common strategic alignment and whether goals are integrated, as conflicts can become barriers to sustainability

questionText: Which of the following is an example of an external driver that can also act as an external barrier?
options: Regulation (can reduce innovation or lead to compliance-only behavior)

questionText: What is the main recommendation for logistics service providers regarding network reviews?
options: Deploy network reviews of large closed networks to ensure efficient hierarchies and nodal structures

questionText: Which of the following is a characteristic of biodegradable packaging for composting?
options: It should hinder the composting process
It should not hinder separation collection and composting, and should decompose into CO2, biomass, and water

questionText: What is the main role of top management commitment in sustainable supply chain strategy?
options: Lack of top management commitment is the most common cause of "island" solutions

questionText: Which of the following is an example of a "Cleaner production" opportunity related to good housekeeping?
options: Using 5S routines to ensure materials are clearly labelled and located, preventing leaks and spills

questionText: What is the main finding regarding the comparison of plastic and alternative packaging materials?
options: Without plastic, the tonnage of alternative materials would increase by a factor of four, GHG emissions by two, costs by 1.9, energy use by 1.5, and waste by 1.9

questionText: Which of the following is a key element of the "Re-design" strategic program?
options: Collaborative approach and quantification of decision-making to assess scenarios, as actions are often high-cost and irreversible

questionText: What is the main purpose of the EU directive requirement that packaging designed for energy recovery have a minimum inferior calorific value?
options: To allow optimization of energy recovery

questionText: Which of the following is a driver for sustainable supply chain practices from investors?
options: Investors pressure companies for better environmental and social performance (mentioned as external driver)
Investors only care about short-term profits

questionText: In the context of cleaner production, what is the main difference between end-of-pipe solutions and integrated preventive strategies?
options: End-of-pipe shifts waste from one medium to another; integrated prevention reduces waste at source

questionText: Which of the following is a recommendation for shippers and buyers to "de-speed" the supply chain?
options: Consider reducing speed to lower carbon emissions, as part of greening logistics

questionText: What is the main advantage of using r-HDPE for milk containers?
options: It can be recycled into plastic pellets for producing milk containers again (closed-loop recycling)

questionText: Which of the following is a key success factor for the "Re-design" strategic program?
options: Collaborative approach and top management commitment

questionText: What is the main purpose of the "Threat-Opportunity Profile" in Step 3?
options: To assess supply chain capabilities in the context of scenarios and determine specific risks and opportunities

questionText: Which of the following is an example of a barrier to sustainable procurement related to cost?
options: Customers are willing to pay a premium
Costs associated with implementation are significant, especially for SMEs, and customers may aim for lowest price

questionText: What is the main recommendation for policy makers regarding green buildings?
options: Encourage industry to commit to improvements considering future technologies through individual and sector-wide actions

questionText: Which of the following is a characteristic of the "Progression" strategic program's benefit?
options: Long-term qualitative benefits related to reputation and image, first mover advantage

questionText: What is the main recommendation for logistics service providers regarding collaboration?
options: Integrate optimization efforts across multiple networks and enable collaboration between multiple shippers and/or carriers

questionText: Which of the following is a key element of the "Innovation" strategic program?
options: Innovation management for new products and supply chain services, training, and profit-sharing models

questionText: What is the main challenge of implementing cleaner production in terms of mindset?
options: It is easy to change mindsets
Industries have to shift away from ignoring pollution and end-of-pipe solutions to preventive strategies

questionText: Which of the following is a driver for sustainable supply chain practices from non-governmental campaigning groups?
options: They can publicly embarrass companies, influencing customers and lawmakers

questionText: What is the main purpose of the "Process Optimizations" strategic program?
options: To improve productivity and efficiency, reducing costs and environmental impacts

questionText: Which of the following is a characteristic of the "Compliance" strategic program?
options: Defensive, precautionary response to stakeholders, focused on risk reduction

questionText: What is the main advantage of using statistical process control (SPC) in cleaner production?
options: It reduces process variations, leading to less rejection and rework

questionText: Which of the following is a recommendation for shippers and buyers regarding sustainable sourcing policies?
options: Ignore carbon impact of primary production
Develop sustainable sourcing policies that consider carbon impact of primary production, manufacturing, and rework

questionText: What is the main purpose of the "six-step approach" as described in the text?
options: To eliminate all supply chain activities
To integrate sustainability principles into an existing supply chain through iterative strategy design and re-design
To focus only on cost reduction

questionText: Which of the following is a key success factor for the "Progression" strategic program regarding external involvement?
options: Active involvement in associations, funding research, and consulting with politics and regulation

questionText: What is the main benefit of using total preventive maintenance (TPM) in cleaner production?
options: It supports standardized operation and maintenance, preventing leaks and improving efficiency

questionText: Which of the following is a recommendation for policy makers regarding freight infrastructure?
options: Make specific investments in congested nodes around road junctions, ports, and rail junctions

questionText: What is the main purpose of the "SSC Scorecard" in Step 5?
options: To help balance economic, environmental, and social objectives and translate strategy into a structured KPI system
To focus only on environmental metrics

questionText: Which of the following is a characteristic of the "Resistant adaptation" regarding laws?
options: Following laws only by letter, with no intrinsic motivation

questionText: What is the main advantage of using bio-polishing and bleach clean-up combined in the Combi process?
options: It saves time, water, energy, and costs

questionText: Which of the following is a recommendation for logistics service providers regarding mode switches?
options: Switch to more environmentally friendly modes within their own networks

questionText: What is the main purpose of the "Balanced Scorecard" in sustainable supply chain strategy?
options: To articulate, communicate, and align initiatives to achieve common goals, not as a controlling system

questionText: Which of the following is a key element of the "Cleaner production" approach regarding product design?
options: Reduce environmental impact of products throughout their lifecycle by designing environmentally friendly but cost-effective products

questionText: What is the main recommendation for shippers and buyers regarding carbon labeling?
options: Work with consumers to better support understanding of carbon footprints and labeling where appropriate
Only label products with high carbon footprint
